description: A stereo turntable: it records what you play into a circular buffer and gives you a platter you can drag, freeze, reverse and slip, or loads a sound file to play instead

params.text: Sets how far back into the recording the playhead may travel, from none of it at the far left to the whole buffer at the far right; with a sample loaded it sets where the playback window ends
Sets the playback speed, half speed at the far left, normal speed at centre and double speed at the far right; a cable in the RATE jack takes this knob out of the calculation entirely
Scales how far a drag on the platter moves the playhead, half as far at the far left and twice as far at the far right
Crossfades the outputs between the signal arriving at IN L and IN R and the sound coming off the buffer, dry at the far left and buffer only at the far right
Mixes the output back into what is being written to the buffer, so material repeats and builds up; at the far left nothing is fed back
Stops the playhead and stops recording, holding whatever is in the buffer; with a cable in the FREEZE jack and Freeze CV set to Gated Control the state follows the cable and this button does nothing
Runs the playhead backwards; with a cable in the REV jack and Reverse CV set to Gated Control the direction follows the cable and this button does nothing
Keeps the recording running underneath while you move the platter, so releasing it returns the playhead to where the sound would have been; the menu sets how quickly it rejoins
Steps through the cartridge characters, which change the tone of the sound read off the platter
Adds a TD.Scope expander to the right of this module

inputs.text: Moves the playhead while the scratch gate is high, one second of recording per volt, positive voltage moving forward toward the newest sound in the buffer and negative deeper into the past
Sets the playback speed, half speed at -10V, normal speed at 0V and double speed at +10V; while a cable is in this jack the RATE knob is ignored, so a cable resting at 0V pins the speed to normal
The left channel of the signal written into the buffer
The right channel of the signal written into the buffer
A voltage above 1V hands the playhead to the POS jack for as long as it is held, and starts the scratch gesture that S.GATE and S.POS report
A voltage above 1V stops the playhead and stops recording; crossing below -1V instead sends the playhead back to the start of the buffer
A voltage above 1V runs the playhead backwards; in Gated Control it holds the direction for as long as it is high, in Pulsed Control each rising edge flips it

outputs.text: The left channel of the mix of the input signal and the sound coming off the buffer, set by WET
10V for as long as a scratch gesture is running, whether it came from dragging the platter, dragging a TD.Scope waveform or the GATE jack, and 0V otherwise
The right channel of the mix of the input signal and the sound coming off the buffer, set by WET
How far the playhead has moved since the scratch gesture began, one volt per second, positive meaning toward the newest sound; it reads 0V whenever S.GATE is low

notes: the round platter is a single drawn widget rather than a control: drag it to move the playhead, and nothing on it can be clicked for its own note
the module records whatever arrives at IN L and IN R from the moment it is placed, so with nothing patched in and no sample loaded there is nothing in the buffer to play
to play a sound file instead of the incoming signal, load it from the menu; the buffer, the platter and every transport control then work on the file
menu: Load sample... — opens a file chooser for a WAV, FLAC or MP3 to play in place of what the module records
Clear sample — discards the loaded file and returns the module to recording its inputs
Convert live -> sample — freezes what is currently in the buffer into a loaded sample, so it stops being overwritten
Save sample... — writes a sample made from the buffer to a WAV file
Sample info — shows the loaded file's name and length, and says so when it was cut short to fit the buffer
Buffer range: 10 s, 20 s, 1 min stereo, 2 min stereo, 10 min stereo, 10 min mono — sets how much recording is held, and so how much memory the module takes
Scratch interpolation: Cubic, 6-point Lagrange, Sinc (CPU heavy) — picks the arithmetic used to read between samples while scratching, trading tone for processor time
HQ rate interpolation — uses the better arithmetic for ordinary playback as well as for scratching
Gate+Pos mode: Module sync, Glide / inertia — sets whether the POS jack snaps the playhead to its voltage or glides toward it
Reverse CV: Gated Control, Pulsed Control — sets whether the REV jack holds the direction while high or flips it on each rising edge
Freeze CV: Gated Control, Pulsed Control — sets whether the FREEZE jack holds the freeze while high or toggles it on each rising edge
Slip return speed: None, Slow, Normal, Instant — sets how quickly the playhead rejoins the newest point in the recording after a slip, or turns slip off
Vinyl — chooses the artwork drawn on the platter and its brightness, and downloads the maker's library of platter art
